aad_spots.name: American Academy of Dermatology: How to fade dark spots

jcs_coconut.name: J Cosmet Sci 2003: oils and hair protein loss (Rele & Mohile)

mja_lime.name: Med J Aust 2017: Phytophotodermatitis from lime juice

actives.name: Benzoyl peroxide
actives.how: Kills acne bacteria and calms inflamed spots.
actives.cautions: Can dry and irritate: start every other day. Bleaches towels, pillowcases and hair. Makes skin more sun-sensitive.

actives.name: Azelaic acid
actives.how: Unclogs pores, calms redness and fades marks; gentler than most acne treatments.
actives.cautions: May sting for the first weeks.

actives.name: Adapalene (a retinoid)
actives.how: Keeps pores from clogging and prevents new spots; one of the most effective topical treatments.
actives.cautions: Dryness and peeling at first; use a pea-sized amount at night and daily sunscreen.

actives.name: Retinol
actives.how: Speeds skin renewal so dark spots fade over months.
actives.cautions: Start 2-3 nights a week; can irritate; use sunscreen every day.

actives.name: Vitamin C (ascorbic acid)
actives.how: An antioxidant that helps fade dark spots and brighten uneven tone.
actives.cautions: Can tingle; store away from light.

actives.name: Glycolic acid
actives.how: Exfoliates the top layer of skin to fade marks.
actives.cautions: Makes skin sun-sensitive; don't combine with retinoids on the same night at first.

actives.name: Kojic acid
actives.how: Reduces pigment production in the skin.
actives.cautions: Can irritate or cause allergy; patch test first.

actives.name: Niacinamide (vitamin B3)
actives.how: Helps control oil, calms redness and evens out tone, with little irritation.
actives.cautions: Higher strengths (10%) can cause flushing in some people.

actives.name: Broad-spectrum sunscreen
actives.how: Prevents sunburn and new dark spots, and helps existing ones fade. Needed on every skin tone.
actives.cautions: Reapply every 2 hours outdoors; use shade and a hat too.

actives.name: Glycerin
actives.strength: any moisturiser with it high on the list
actives.how: Draws water into the skin.
actives.cautions: None for most people.

actives.name: Hyaluronic acid
actives.how: Holds water in the skin; best under a cream.
actives.cautions: None for most people.

actives.name: Petrolatum or an emollient ointment
actives.how: Seals moisture in and protects the skin barrier.
actives.cautions: Can feel greasy; paraffin products are flammable on fabrics.

actives.name: Ceramides
actives.how: Rebuild the skin's natural barrier lipids.
actives.cautions: None for most people.

actives.name: Shea butter
actives.how: A rich emollient that softens dry skin.
actives.cautions: Rarely, allergy in people with tree-nut sensitivity.

actives.name: Ketoconazole shampoo
actives.how: Treats the yeast that drives dandruff; one of the most effective options.
actives.cautions: Leave on 3-5 minutes before rinsing; use twice a week.

actives.name: Zinc pyrithione
actives.how: Reduces the scalp yeast behind flaking.
actives.cautions: None for most people.

actives.name: Selenium sulfide
actives.how: Slows flaking and reduces scalp yeast.
actives.cautions: Can discolour dyed or grey hair; rinse well.

actives.name: Salicylic acid
actives.how: Loosens thick flakes so they wash away.
actives.cautions: Can dry the scalp; follow with conditioner.

actives.name: Coal tar
actives.how: Slows the skin turnover that causes heavy flaking.
actives.cautions: Strong smell; can stain light hair; makes scalp sun-sensitive.

actives.name: Minoxidil
actives.how: The main over-the-counter treatment for pattern hair loss in men and women.
actives.cautions: Takes 4-6 months; some extra shedding at first; regrowth is lost if you stop.

actives.name: Finasteride (men only)
actives.how: A tablet for male pattern hair loss.
actives.cautions: Prescription only; women must not take it or handle broken tablets.

actives.name: Coconut oil (before washing)
actives.how: Reduces protein loss from hair during washing, so hair breaks less.
actives.cautions: Doesn't regrow hair; can worsen dandruff on an oily scalp.

irritants.name: Fragrance
irritants.why: The most common cause of skin allergy from cosmetics.

irritants.name: Essential oils
irritants.why: Natural, but often irritating or allergenic; some citrus oils react with sunlight.

irritants.name: Drying alcohol
irritants.why: Can dry and irritate, especially high on the list of a leave-on product.

irritants.name: Menthol
irritants.why: The cooling feel can irritate sensitive skin.

irritants.name: Methylisothiazolinone
irritants.why: A preservative that is a common cause of contact allergy.

irritants.name: Sodium lauryl sulfate
irritants.why: A strong foaming cleanser that can dry and irritate skin.
